sentences.text:
1 It is the preliminary argument of the learned counsel for the appellant that as per the address of the appellant given in the complaint, the appellant lives in Prayagraj district and the opposite party no.
2 lives in district Kaushambi.
As the appellant is living in separate district, the Magistrate was bound to make an inquiry under Section 202 (1) Cr.P.C. before passing the impugned order.

If we go through the complaint, which is appended at page-5 of the paper book, the address of the complainant/opposite party no. 2 is of Kaushambi district and the address of the appellant (opposite party in the complaint) is of District Prayagraj.

Thus, in the light of Section 202 (1) Cr.P.C. which is a mandatory section, the trial court was bound to inquire into the case either himself or he could direct for investigation to be done by the police officer or by such person as he thinks fit for the purpose of deciding whether or not there is sufficient ground for proceeding.

Thus, in the opinion of the court, in the complaint itself the opposite party no. 2 has mentioned the address of the appellant Aun Raza showing him to be resident of district Prayagraj, then he cannot deviate from his assertion.

At page-31 of the counter affidavit, the address of Muzaffari Fatma,
mother of the appellant, is also shown of district Prayagraj.
When the opposite party no. 2 himself has mentioned the address of the appellant and the address of the mother of the appellant of district Prayagraj, he cannot deviate from his admission.

In the opinion of the court, as the appellant lives in different district so the inquiry was mandatory as per Section 202(1) Cr.P.C., which is not shown to be done by the trial court as per impugned order.
Hence, the appeal is allowed.
The impugned order dated 19.05.2022 is set aside.

The trial court is directed to pass a fresh order after making an inquiry, as per Section 202(1) Cr.P.C.
within three months from the date of receiving a certified copy of this order.
The trial court is further directed to make it clear as to how a person is being summoned under Section 3(1)10 of SC/ST Act, while no such section exists in the Act after year, 2016.
